Execute Final SoupX Contamination Removal and Seurat Initialization

Source: R/Pre-processing_soupX.R
run_soupx_post_clustering.Rd

The second half of the master ambient RNA removal workflow. It takes the bundled preparation data (generated by prepare_soupx_inputs), estimates the contamination fractions using the high-resolution clusters, applies any specified manual overrides, and adjusts the count matrices. Finally, it automatically initializes a fresh list of Seurat objects using the decontaminated counts, returning a comprehensive list of all objects generated during the process.

Usage

run_soupx_post_clustering(
  prep_output,
  multiFac = 0,
  manual_contam = list(),
  pCut = 0.01,
  methods = "subtraction"
)

Arguments

prep_output

A structured list containing sample_names, soup_list, seurat_for_clustering, and counts_lists. Typically the direct output of prepare_soupx_inputs().

multiFac

Numeric. A percentage to artificially add to the auto-estimated contamination fraction (rho). Default is 0.

manual_contam

Character vector. An optional list of specific sample names to selectively apply the multiFac adjustment to. Default is an empty list.

pCut

Numeric. The p-value threshold used for identifying cells expressing genes above background levels when methods = "soupOnly". Default is 0.01.

methods

Character. The method to use for count adjustment passed to SoupX::adjustCounts(). Options include "subtraction", "soupOnly", or "multinomial". Default is "subtraction".

Value

A structured, named list containing three top-level elements:

  • final_seurat: A list of the final, initialized Seurat objects containing the background-corrected counts and baseline metadata (e.g., mitoPercent).

  • soup_objects: A list of the updated SoupChannel objects with their calculated rho values.

  • seurat_clustering: A list of the preliminary Seurat objects used to generate the high-resolution clusters for estimation.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# 1. Run the preparation phase
soupx_prep_data <- prepare_soupx_inputs(
  filtered_dir = "data/cellranger/filtered",
  raw_dir = "data/cellranger/raw"
)

# 2. Execute the contamination removal and generate final Seurat objects
final_pipeline_output <- run_soupx_post_clustering(
  prep_output = soupx_prep_data,
  multiFac = 2,                 # Add 2% extra contamination penalty
  manual_contam = c("Donor_A"), # Only apply the penalty to Donor_A
  methods = "subtraction"
)

# 3. Extract your final cleaned Seurat objects for downstream integration
my_clean_seurats <- final_pipeline_output$final_seurat
} # }
